ctl-a.claim: round-50 entry bytes at the C2 path plus two new rows -> must MISS via clause (c)

ctl-a2.claim: round-50 entry bytes with the source/held block replaced by the scaffold rows and three valid held citations -> (a)(b)(d) pass and only clause (c) misses

ctl-b.claim: round-49 candidate at the C2 path -> must MISS via clause (c)

ctl-b2.claim: round-49 candidate with the source/held block replaced by the scaffold rows and three valid held citations -> (a)(b)(d) pass and only clause (c) misses

ctl-c.claim: new entry with held citations whose pinned tokens are absent from the cited lines -> must MISS via clause (d)

ctl-d.claim: new entry citing rows S364/S365 whose pin files are absent -> must MISS via clause (b)

ctl-e.claim: bare round base - entry absent -> must MISS (admitted=0/1, exit 1)

notes: clauses are the probe's frozen-sentence reading; counter_clauses are the draft counter's own a/b/c/d lines
ctl-e's probe clause (c) is vacuously true on an absent entry (zero shingles); the counter skips b-d when the entry is absent, so its vector is all zeros

ctl-a/ctl-b are byte-reuse controls, not clause-isolating: the copied bytes also fail (b) and (d). ctl-a2/ctl-b2 add the isolation by rewriting only the source/held block, leaving the copied body intact
